methodological_rigor.justification: The study has a fundamental design flaw: the 'pediatric' class is represented by a single cell line (SF188) versus five adult lines, so the classifier is essentially learning the SF188 signature rather than a generalizable pediatric vs adult signature — the authors acknowledge this but it undermines the central claim. The train/test split is said to be stratified at the spectrum level with 'no spectra from a given cell shared,' but with only one pediatric line all pediatric training and test spectra originate from the same biological source, which is leakage at the biological-replicate level. The reported cross-validation accuracy (~66%) is markedly lower than the held-out test accuracy (83.6%), a discrepancy the authors do not reconcile. Statistically, no confidence intervals are reported for accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, or specificity; no power calculation, no bootstrapping, no permutation test, and no multiplicity correction for spectral band comparisons are described. Biological/technical replicate structure (per-cell vs per-line) is not formalized, and there is no sensitivity analysis across cell lines.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical in vitro study on patient-derived GBM neurosphere lines, which maps to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/basic science). The clinical question — rapid intraoperative distinction of pediatric vs adult GBM — is relevant, but the translational path from spectra of CaF2-mounted cell suspensions to tissue/in-situ measurements is long and the authors explicitly flag this. With only one pediatric line, the demonstrated classifier cannot be considered diagnostically meaningful; the manuscript is a feasibility/proof-of-concept with speculative near-term clinical impact.

reporting_quality.justification: No formal reporting checklist cleanly applies to a preclinical in vitro Raman+ML study; ARRIVE is for animal work, TRIPOD could partially apply as a prediction-model guide but is not followed systematically. Instrument, acquisition parameters, preprocessing (baseline, normalization, Savitzky–Golay), MLP architecture search, and PCA retention are described with reasonable detail, but TRIPOD-style items are missing: no sample-size justification, no reporting of model calibration, no CIs around performance, no handling of missing/excluded spectra counts, and biological-replicate structure is not clearly tabulated. The blinded manuscript contains no data-availability or code-availability statement, no repository link, no reference to a code platform, and no supplementary materials sufficient for independent replication.

novelty_literature.justification: The methodological combination (confocal Raman + MLP) is well-established, and prior Raman/ML work on glioma (refs 11, 17, 22) and on pediatric brain tumors specifically (refs 28–30, 62) is extensive and cited. The specific framing — pediatric vs adult GBM stem-like cells — is a new empirical slice, but the novelty is undermined by using a single pediatric line, making this closer to a 'spectral profiling of SF188 against a panel of adult lines' than a true pediatric-vs-adult discovery. Positioning is reasonable and the authors appropriately hedge the 'first' claim in the discussion.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized conventionally and the abstract conveys the main numbers (n=1,382 spectra, 83.6% accuracy, AUC 0.855, 91.4% pediatric sensitivity). However, there are multiple typographic and grammatical errors ('metholody', 'challanged', 'metabolsim', 'perfomring', 'ouf', 'G34R/Vsubstitutions', 'modularly tailoring'), and some sentences are awkward (e.g., 'relative to other tested architectures during cross-validation accuracy and simplicity'). Figure captions are terse and do not stand alone (e.g., Figure 4 caption does not describe the methodology schematic). The discussion is appropriately self-critical about the single pediatric line limitation.

key_strengths: Clear acknowledgment in the discussion that findings reflect the SF188 phenotype rather than pediatric GBM broadly
Reasonably detailed Raman acquisition parameters (532 nm, 20 mW, 20 s integration, CaF2 substrate, 600–1800 cm^-1 fingerprint range)
Explicit train/test separation with preprocessing (StandardScaler, PCA) fit on training data only to avoid leakage at the preprocessing level
Clinically motivated question — rapid intraoperative stratification of pediatric vs adult high-grade glioma
key_concerns: Single pediatric cell line (SF188) vs five adult lines: the classifier cannot distinguish a 'pediatric signature' from an 'SF188 signature,' and all pediatric train and test spectra share the same biological source
Large gap between 10-fold CV accuracy (~66%) and held-out test accuracy (83.6%) is unexplained and raises concerns about the independence of the held-out spectra
No confidence intervals for accuracy/AUC/sensitivity/specificity, no bootstrapping, no permutation test, no multiplicity correction for band-wise comparisons, no power or sample-size justification
No data-availability or code-availability statement, no repository, no supplementary materials for independent replication
Spectral-to-biology attributions (TP53, lipid rafts, cytochromes) are speculative and not supported by orthogonal biochemical assays
Multiple typographic/grammatical errors and uninformative figure captions reduce clarity
chief_reviewer.rationale: A preliminary proof-of-concept whose central claim (pediatric vs adult discrimination) is undermined by a single pediatric cell line and limited statistical reporting; competent execution within those limits suggests a low-tier venue after major revisions that add additional pediatric lines, performance CIs, and code/data sharing.
